properties.project_name: P11 -- landscaped median strip connecting Mission Bay Circle to P11A
properties.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery, guided directly by the owner's own marked-up screenshot (their drawn outline extracted from the photo via ORB feature-matching/homography), then fit to an idealized road-aligned rectangle per the owner's description of the real shape.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-19: resolves plan label P11. This session had first wrongly attributed P11 to a distant, already-tracked 'Mission Bay Commons' record near Illinois St, inferred only from a source note that gave build years (not locations) for P11/P16/P17 as a group -- the owner's own drawing showed P11 right here instead, next to P11A, contradicting that location inference (P16/P17 were left as-is per the owner's instruction; only P11 corrected). The owner's blue outline was extracted from their annotated photo via ORB keypoint matching (a homography to the original sent image, chained to a second homography to a freshly-fetched satellite tile with a known exact lon/lat extent), avoiding manual pixel-guessing. The owner then described the real shape as a thin rectangle aligned with the road; a minimum-area rotated rectangle was fit to the extracted outline (4.8m x 63.1m, angle -87.5 deg from east) rather than left as the noisier hand-traced outline. This is the tree-lined median strip connecting the roundabout named 'Mission Bay Circle' in this tracker (near P8/P10/X1) east to the P11A half-circle island. join_approximate.py --strict flagged 100% clip against the real street/curb buffer -- expected and correct here, not a mispositioning: this median sits entirely within the road right-of-way (that's the whole point of a traffic median), so DataSF's curb layer legitimately treats its full footprint as street. The owner granted an explicit exception (same reasoning as P11A) rather than have this shape zeroed out by the generic clip. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: no source was cited for this feature; source_doc_urls now lists the OCII Sept 2023 transition presentation (lists 'P11/11A' among parcels RPD will manage), the OCII Dec 2019 Land Use Map (labels P11 then P11A east of P10/Mission Bay Circle, per the audit reviewers), the OCII Nov 2024 CAC update and SF Rec & Park's Workshop 3 deck. These support the P11 location and 'park' use but not the strip's physical description, which rests on this repository's own trace. The identification of this median as P11 remains the owner's; the Nov 2024 CAC update and the Workshop 3 deck ('P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)') group P11 with the Mission Bay Commons, so the owner should settle what P11 covers.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- owner-guided satellite trace, idealized to a fitted rectangle rather than left as a raw hand-traced outline. Not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team. street_clip_exempt=true: this is a real median strip that sits entirely within the paved road right-of-way by design -- clipping it against the generic street buffer would zero it out entirely, not correct a mispositioning. Owner-approved exception.
properties.p_number: P11. OCII's Nov 2024 CAC update (src-ocii-openspace-2024) groups P11 with P12, P13, P15, P16 and P17 as 'Mission Bay Commons', and SF Rec & Park's Workshop 3 deck (p.15) lists 'P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)'; OCII's Dec 2019 Land Use Map and the Nov 2024 p.2 map are reported to label P11 just east of Mission Bay Circle, where this strip is. Whether P11 is this median strip or a larger Commons segment is unresolved (owner).
properties.notes: Thin landscaped median strip with a row of trees, connecting the Mission Bay Circle roundabout to the P11A median island.
